title: Tower Defense
text: “That’s just how much of an object of envy becoming a hero’s companion is.”
“At first, I genuinely thought, what kind of joke is this?”
“I get why you’d doubt it… but it really was true, and thanks to that I’ve been given power and circumstances far beyond what I deserve.”
“The problem is… even with all that power, there’s not much opportunity to actually use it…”
For some reason the slaves glanced at me just then. What, indeed?
“Even so, I’m no match for a hero.”
Perhaps this was a good moment to share a little story, I thought.
“By the way, I did mention this to Father at the very start, but in other loops, you two were each bought individually by Father, separately.”
“That’s right. Apparently there were loops where everyone but Wolf got bought.”
“Hoh…”
“I wonder how that version of me differs from this one? Hard to picture it, isn’t it.”
“Vof?”
Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy leaned in, looking interested.
“To be specific, there was a reason I couldn’t save Father from the false charges that time. I was keeping a discreet watch, but Father ended up just as wild as he was in the very first world.”
“Ah, that’s the ‘Wild’ state Gaelion keeps talking about. So he got bought while in that state?”
“Indeed. Alone, in that case.”
“A solo purchase, huh.”
“Well, that loop only lasted from a few days after the duel until roughly the point Filo-tan came to be, so.”
“Only that far, huh… Either way, I’m curious, so keep going.”

Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy nodded, urging me on. Naturally, my eyes drifted to Father as well. Wolf, unable to join the conversation, tried to inch closer to Father, only to be blocked by Crocodile Guy and the others.
“Though, honestly, there wasn’t much difference. When Rabbit Guy was chosen, his duel opponent was Itsuki, who denounced Father. When it was Crocodile Guy, it was Ren.”
“That situation again, huh.”
“So blatant. That princess.”
“You two seemed to be having some secret conversation…”
“Ah, Crocodile Guy didn’t seem to know Éclair was being held captive that time. Still, he snapped and managed to reach his current form. Rabbit Guy also talked back to Itsuki quite fiercely.”
“How should I put it…”
Rabbit Guy stared intently at Father.
“Part of me is a little envious of that version of me, and part of me thinks the way things are now is better. Complicated feelings, really.”
“What kind of feeling is that? No… well, I guess I get something similar, hearing about all these different loop-versions of me from Motoyasu-kun.”
“There was a girl Big Sister and Spear Hero mentioned calling out to. Was she around in that loop too?”
“In the very first world, it was Big Sister that Father purchased. There were three purchased as slaves in total.”
“Myself, Theo, and that girl, huh…”
“It makes you feel fate at work, for better or worse. I’ll give credit where it’s due on this one, at least. Though there was talk of being remembered and all that.”
Rabbit Guy was looking rather smug about something. You won’t beat me in cuteness, rabbit or not, I say.
“Nothing for me.”
“Wolf’s too expensive—that Father couldn’t have afforded him.”
“Vof… too bad. Then I’ll work hard.”
“At what?”
“Voff-!”
Wolf seemed to dodge the question with a bark.
“One more question, okay?”
“What is it?”
“Can you save my brother?”
Wolf’s brother, was it? From what I understood, Takt’s seizure of the Claw’s Seven Star Weapon apparently happened before the waves even began.
“I don’t think that’s possible. The furthest back I can return to is right after the summoning. If it were Big Sister’s friend, I could have saved her, but…”
Even this loop had barely made it in time to save Father at the earliest point the Spear Spirit had determined I could loop back to.
“…Vof. What Takt did to me happened way before then… so, impossible, huh.”
Father set a hand gently on Wolf’s drooping shoulder.
“I can imagine how you feel.”
“Vof.”
“…Yeah. If I could go back before the waves started with the strength I have now… I think about that too. If there were someone capable of it, I’d want to entrust it to them.”
“…In that sense, I suppose I was fortunate to have nothing like that, until I met Iwatani-sama and the others.”
“That’s a bit heavy… Theo’s not entirely without baggage either… Anyway, let’s change the subject—Wolf was quite the reader, and there are plenty of books here.”
Father checked out the study in Wolf’s house.
“So, is Wolf’s prized antique book somewhere in here? Or was it in the room we just saw?”
“Vof, this.”
Saying that, Wolf pulled out a tattered, faded book from deep within the study shelves.
“Wow… that’s really beat up.”
“What is it?”
“First edition biography of Mamoru, the Shield Hero.”
“Wha—what did you say?”
Theo’s eyes changed color at once. He looked at the book’s cover with something like trepidation as Wolf held it out.
“Something that incredible still exists…? That’s a piece of history thought lost forever!”
“It’s that amazing a find?”
“Of course it is! There are countless copies stitched together from transcriptions and reproductions, but an actual first edition—there’s no telling how ancient a relic that is!”
“Voff!”
Wolf gave a little snort, as if to say, how do you like that!
“Is it genuine? There are so many forgeries out there it’s almost suspicious.”

“The storage conditions were good, so it’s in decent shape. The contents describe the founding of Siltvelt. It also touches on the waves, but based on my own experience taking part in them, the details differ—so I figure it’s just a biography, take it with a grain of salt. Voff.”
“Protect… fits a Shield Hero kind of name. Heh… so that’s the name of the hero who founded Siltvelt?”
“So the legend says.”

Rabbit Guy took the book from Wolf, looking hesitant, and opened it to check the contents, so I peeked over as well. …The characters resembled Siltvelt script, but were different in various ways. Felt like old Japanese classical writing. Reading it at a glance seemed impossible.
“The waves were different, you said?”

“Vof, something about… a ritual to clear a death game hosted by someone claiming to be a god, and defending a base from an endless line of monsters—among the heroes’ tales, it’s described as something called ‘tawer-difensu’? Tower defense, I guess.”

“The first part… kind of sounds close to what Motoyasu-kun told me, but more like a death game. The second one, tower defense—well, that also sounds kind of like a wave, in a way. It’s a bit different, but also not really?”
“Not very useful as reference material. It’s written as though they lost to the wave and a new world spread out—but the world didn’t end.”
“True, most accounts tend to end with ‘overcame the disaster,’ but here it’s treated as a loss?”
Well, given that world fusion apparently occurs from events in the very first world during the waves, I suppose the world would survive even in defeat.

“The design of this ‘god’ figure is also strange. It’s drawn as something wearing a mask resembling a Beastman, but not actually a Beastman—and it’s depicted as being finished off by an unusual Beastman. The Claw Hero, maybe?”

Right about here, Wolf took the book back from Rabbit Guy and spread open the illustrated page in question. Most of it was faded, but… I could make it out—there was Ark, wearing what looked like a gentleman’s outfit with a cat mask, being sliced into three pieces by a claw strike. The coloring was off, wasn’t it? No, even the fur volume seemed different somehow. Who drew this? Still, it seemed broadly accurate, somehow.

Though, I felt it was probably better not to talk too much about Ark. Speaking of which… there was one thing I suddenly recalled about Ark. For some reason, everyone perceived Ark’s fur color and fur volume differently. Someone in the village had said black, while others said white, yellow, rust-colored, short-haired, long-haired, and so on—it varied from person to person. Why was that, I wonder?

Hou-kun, at least, had recognized the same design as everyone else, so I didn’t think it was some trait of the god-slayer specifically. Everyone recognized it as Ark, and yet what each person actually saw wasn’t uniform, so to speak. Well, the lizard-like fur-covered tail was universally recognized as the defining feature. Truly a mysterious fellow, I say.
